items.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: It was taught to me by Don Cherry when I worked with Don Cherry. He taught me “Bemsha Swing”

ctx.x: It was taught to me by Don Cherry when I worked with Don Cherry. He taught me “Bemsha Swing” and this was the bass line [scats]. You know so this bass line comes from “Bemsha Swing” and what I did was just superimpose another melody on the top of it because it’s a great bass line for the tuba. A lot of my things that I choose to do are bass

line kind of driven. The only one composition I’ve written that wasn’t and that was a song for my son called “CJ” and it just — the melody came to me while watching him move around the house, where he — it’s in seven and then it switches back to six. So I mean you see him walking and he’s like —
